title: Identity Trial Capture
statement: Let $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$ be Boolean finite-state Turing machines, let $x$ and $u$ be Boolean words, and let $t,s$ be natural numbers. Suppose $M_I$ halts on $x$ after $t$ steps with output $x$, and uses at most $s$ work-tape cells by time $t$. Then the identity-phase machine, started in the initial cleaning state with input-head position $1$, the first tape storing $u$, and its other tapes blank, reaches a configuration at some time $T$ with some input-head position $p$, the first tape still storing $u$, the second storing $x$, and the third blank. It avoids its designated exit state at every earlier time, and every work-tape head throughout the run has absolute position at most $|x|+s$.
